title: Palindrome Linked List
statement: Return True if the values of a singly linked list read the same forwards and backwards. Try to use O(1) extra space.
reference_solution:
def isPalindrome(head):
    slow = fast = head
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
    prev = None
    while slow:
        nxt = slow.next
        slow.next = prev
        prev = slow
        slow = nxt
    a, b = head, prev
    while b:
        if a.val != b.val:
            return False
        a = a.next
        b = b.next
    return True

hints.1_question: A palindrome reads the same from both ends, but a singly linked list only goes one direction. How could you compare the second half backwards?
hints.2_nudge: Find the middle with slow/fast pointers, reverse the second half in place, then compare it with the first half.
hints.3_big_hint: Middle: slow/fast. Reverse from slow to the end. Walk a from head and b from the reversed half while b exists, comparing values.

known_bugs.name: splits the value list in half without reversing
known_bugs.code:
def isPalindrome(head):
    vals = []
    while head:
        vals.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    h = len(vals) // 2
    return vals[:h] == vals[h:]
known_bugs.followup: For [1,2,2,1] you compare [1,2] with [2,1]. Should the second half be read in the same order or reversed?
